chunks: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
“The Day We shall call every people by their Imam.”

So he said: “O Fuḍayl, know your Imam, for when you know your Imam, it will not harm you whether this matter comes sooner or is delayed. And whoever knows his Imam, then dies before the Master of this matter rises, is at the rank of one who was sitting in his army—rather, at the rank of one who sat beneath his banner.”
He said: “And some of his companions said: at the rank of one who was martyred with Rasūl Allāh صلى الله عليه وآله.”
Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Jumhūr, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:

key_terms.إِمَامَكَ: your Imam; the divinely designated leader whose recognition is essential
key_terms.اسْتُشْهِدَ: was martyred; attained shahādah in the path of Allah
key_terms.صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the Master of this matter; the Qāʾim associated with the awaited rising
key_terms.عَسْكَرِهِ: his army; the company and ranks of the Imam’s supporters
key_terms.لِوَائِهِ: his banner; a symbol of allegiance and nearness to the Imam
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرُ: this matter; the divinely appointed cause associated with the Imam’s rise

ai.seo_question: Why does recognizing one’s Imam matter even before the rise of Ṣāḥِبُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse about people being called with their Imam on the Day of Judgment by emphasizing the necessity of recognizing the true Imam. It teaches that maʿrifah of the Imam is decisive, and that one who dies with this recognition before the rise of Ṣāḥib al-Amr still attains the rank of those aligned with him. The narration highlights both the doctrinal significance of Imamate and its eschatological consequence.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasar who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High [17:71] The Day when We will Call every human being with their Imam.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Fuzayl! Recognise your Imam<sup>asws</sup>, for you, when you recognise your Imam<sup>asws</sup>, it would not harm you whether this matter is brought forwards or is delayed. And the one who recognises his Imam<sup>asws</sup>, then dies before the rising of the Master of this Command, would be at the status of the one who was seated among his<sup>asws</sup> soldiers. No! But, seated beneath his<sup>asws</sup> flag’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Some of his<sup>asws</sup> companions would be at the status of the ones who were martyred with Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Marwan from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following.
“I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, “On the day when We call every nation with their leaders, Imams. .” [17:71].

He said, “O Fudayl find out who your Imam is because when you will find out who your Imam is then whether this matter (the rise of al-Mahdi with Divine Authority) will take place earlier or later will not affect you at all. One who finds out who his Imam is and then dies before the rise of al-Mahdi with Divine Authority he will be just as those who are positioned in his army. In fact, just like those who have placed themselves under his banner.”
The narrator has said that certain persons from his companions said, “He will be just like the martyrs in battle supporting the Messenger of Allah. “
